1

 Oral Judgment

1. The present acquittal Appeal has been filed by the R/CR.A/1835/2005 JUDGMENT appellant - original complainant under Section 378 (4) of Cr. P.C., against the Judgment and order dated 22.6.2004, rendered in P.F.A. Case No.46 of 1996 by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Municipal Court, Surat.

entities.text:
Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Municipal Court, Surat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The said case was registered against the present respondent No.1 original accused for the offence under sections 2(1-a)(a), 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "PFA Act").
2. The complainant Food Inspector visited on 24.1.1996 at about 9:45 a.m., and took sample of Sev for analysis purpose in the presence of panch and after following due procedure of sealing, packing etc., the same was sent to the Laboratory for analysis purpose and the report of public analyst found adulterated.
Upon receipt of the report, the complainant after obtaining sanction, filed complaint against the respondents original accused for the alleged offence.
Therefore, aforesaid Criminal Case was registered.
3. At the conclusion of trial and after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence, the learned trial Judge vide impugned Judgment, acquitted the respondent - accused.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Shah , appearing on behalf of the appellant has contended that the Judgment and order of acquittal is contrary to law and evidence on record and is not proper.

He has contended that learned trial Judge has not R/CR.A/1835/2005 JUDGMENT appreciated that there is no standard specified in the Act for Sev, but the groundnut oil used, was of sub-standard and of poor quality and therefore, as per the report, the sample of Sev was not as per the standard.
He has also contended that the offences punishable under the Act are directly connected with the health of public at large.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Dave for the respondent - accused supported the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and he submitted that learned trial Judge has rightly appreciated the evidence produced on record and therefore, no interference is required to be called for.
He lastly submitted that present appeal may kindly be dismissed by confirming the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

In this regard, learned advocate also cited the decisions of this Court i.e. 2012(0) GLHEL- HC 227221, 2011(0) GLHEL-HC 223492, 2011(0) GLHEL-HC 223492 and 2012(0)
GLHEL-HC227492.
6.

Heard learned APP Mrs. Hansa Punani for the respondent No.2.
7.
I have gone through the papers produced in the case.
I have also gone through the evidence led before the trial Court as well as the Expert Opinion.
I have also gone through the Judgment of the trial Court.
The learned Magistrate has rightly observed that the standard of the item i.e. Sev has not R/CR.A/1835/2005 JUDGMENT prescribed in Appendix B and same was not found adulterated.
In the facts of the case I am in complete agreement with the reasons assigned by the trial Court.
In view of this position, I am of the view that present case is covered up by the decisions cited by the learned advocate Mr. Dave for the respondent - accused.
Hence, the appeal is required to be dismissed.
